dod_intent_evidence: Two Air Force SBIR Phase II awards (2022, $1.5M + $750K) for AFNWC/DoD technology-forecasting tools, with own abstract stating offerings 'have been fine-tuned by closely working with key DoD stakeholders' — SBIR/STTR record section.
score_evidence: 'Patented algorithms (US Patent US012099572B2), Proprietary Machine Learning models... 20 years of research at MIT' — pure academic/patent-pedigree brag → lab_language_intensity

Detailed abstracts describe 150,000+ technology taxonomy, citation-network algorithms, and weapon-system vulnerability forecasting with zero mention of ATO/RMF/CMMC/ITAR/STIG anywhere on site or in SBIR text → deployment_awareness_absence

Only engagement signal is 'Current TechNext offerings have been fine-tuned by closely working with key DoD stakeholders' — no CONOPS, no named operator, no field-feedback loop described → operator_absence
'no jobs data found' → hiring_profile_skew set to 10 per rule

3-5 employees, two Air Force Phase II awards closed in 2022, and the company's most recent public news (Sept 2025) is a partnership with a commercial semiconductor coalition rather than any DoD program office → stage_pressure

blind_spots.blind_spot: No ATO/RMF or network-authorization pathway described for a tool meant to run inside AFNWC/DoD program-management workflows
blind_spots.operator_reality: A SaaS analytics tool touching DoD technology-portfolio data needs an ATO to actually be installed on a .mil network; 'TechNext's tools can allow AFNWC and DoD stakeholders at large to search, catalog, explore' is aspirational marketing unless there's an accredited deployment behind it
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: team is optimizing forecasting algorithms, not the accreditation pathway to get the tool onto a government network
blind_spots.evidence_quote: TechNext's tools can allow AFNWC and DoD stakeholders at large to search, catalog, explore and anticipate directional technological progress and potential for innovation for any technology

blind_spots.blind_spot: No data-handling/CMMC/NIST 800-171 story despite the Phase II 'Forecasting Future Technological Threats' abstract explicitly analyzing 'vulnerabilities in weapon systems that can be exploited by adversaries'
blind_spots.operator_reality: That kind of adversary-vulnerability analysis is CUI-adjacent at minimum; running it through a 3-5 person company's own infrastructure without a stated compliance posture is exactly the gap that kills a Phase II-to-III transition on a security review
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: company markets its dataset and algorithms, not its own facility/data-handling compliance
blind_spots.evidence_quote: TechNext will build a Technology Crossover Scenario-modeling Tool to identify vulnerabilities in weapon systems that can be exploited by adversaries

blind_spots.blind_spot: No named champion or transition milestone four years after the 2022 Phase II awards; the most recent public partnership (2025) is with a commercial semiconductor coalition, not AFNWC
blind_spots.operator_reality: This is the valley of death in real time: DoD stakeholders liking the tool during Phase II development isn't the same as a program office funding a Phase III or program of record — and the company's public attention has visibly shifted to commercial revenue instead
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: commercial partnerships are easier to close and announce than a DoD program-of-record transition, so the company's growth story naturally drifts commercial
blind_spots.evidence_quote: MIT Startup TechNext Partners with Northeast Microelectronics Coalition to Accelerate Technology Commercialization

opener_hook: TechNext's two Air Force Phase II SBIRs closed in 2022 — its most recent public partnership, in September 2025, is with a commercial semiconductor coalition, not an Air Force program office.
what_they_do: An MIT spin-off selling a patented AI/patent-data platform that forecasts technology performance-improvement rates for R&D and investment decisions, originally developed under Air Force SBIR funding for AFNWC technology forecasting.
